items.title: Stanley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: I had an English friend who was recording, called Dennis Preston, he made quite a few records for him which were issued on English Columbia. ... subsequently I made a lot of records for Dennis Preston’s label in England, English Columbia.

ctx.x: But the records did reasonably well. There was beginners luck in part too, because some, where my heart was really in, didn’t come out so well, but others came out very well. So I go back and these are issued in Europe, with quite good reviews etcetera. And the following year, my wife never really got used to the English climate, and then we were living in a house that was 400 years old you know. And of course the property after World War II in England was at a premium. My father’s house opposite where we lived…
the concert ends, and you’d get down there and you’ve got to write the piece in about 20 minutes.
